There is a reason so many people are confused about the millennium, and it is not by accident. We go straight to Scripture to uncover what the Bible actually says, stripping away traditions, church systems, and popular teachings that have quietly reshaped the truth over time. What emerges is a picture that looks very different from what most have been told. Instead of Christ setting up a kingdom on this fallen earth, the Bible reveals a sequence where the righteous are raised or transformed and caught up to meet Him in the air, while the earth itself is left desolate, empty, and completely undone at His coming. 

This changes everything. It means there is no earthly utopia before restoration, no human effort that can establish God’s kingdom here, and no coexistence of the righteous and the wicked once Christ returns. The idea that we can build a perfect world or hand a kingdom back to God is not just flawed, it opens the door to deception. Scripture shows that the wicked are destroyed at His coming, the earth becomes a wilderness without life, and Satan is bound not by chains in a literal sense, but by circumstance, trapped on a ruined planet with no one left to deceive. 

During this thousand year period, the redeemed are not on earth at all. They are with Christ in heaven, participating in judgment, reviewing the record of what has taken place. Meanwhile, the dead remain in the grave until the end of the thousand years, when the final events unfold. The New Jerusalem descends, the wicked are raised, and Satan makes one last attempt to deceive before everything is brought to its final end. Only after this does the true restoration happen, a new heaven and a new earth where righteousness dwells.

This is not just a theological detail. It is a line of truth that protects against one of the greatest end time deceptions, the idea of a false kingdom on earth and a counterfeit Christ walking among men. If you do not know that the real Christ does not touch the earth at His return, you are vulnerable to believing the wrong one when he appears. That is why this matters. Not tradition. Not what sounds good. But what is actually written.
fulltitle: The Millennium is NOT What You Think According to the Bible
